overall: The AG found no violation for the unanswered April 1 email, which was not filed on the complaint form, and declined to review the untimely allegations about the unread comment and alleged discriminatory motive.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board failed to respond within 14 business days to an April 1 email about not reading a comment in full at the March 24 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find no violation where a public body is not obligated to address a complaint that is not filed using the Attorney General’s Open Meeting Law complaint form.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board violated the law by declining to read a written public comment in full at its March 24 meeting while reading other comments in full.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require a chair to read aloud comments that are submitted to the public body in writing.

allegations.summary: Alleged the Board's reason for not reading the comment in full was discriminatory.
allegations.key_passage: allegations of bias and discrimination would not, in and of themselves, constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law.
